title: Coulomb transversality alone does not supply the Lorentz null numerator on near-parallel rays

current_mismatch.transverse_symbol: For a Coulomb polarization e dot p=0, the spatial current symbol contracts as e dot (2k+p)=2 e dot k
current_mismatch.near_parallel_ray: Take p=(1,0,0), e=(0,1,0), k=(K,1,0); the current numerator is exactly two
current_mismatch.phase_asymptotic: On this ray Phi is asymptotic to (M^2+1)/(2K^2)
current_mismatch.quotient_asymptotic: The transverse-current homological quotient is asymptotic to 4K^2/(M^2+1), retaining the two-derivative loss
current_mismatch.interpretation: Transversality kills the exactly parallel ray but not fixed-offset near-parallel rays and therefore does not reproduce N0
current_mismatch.ceiling: A full Lorentz null decomposition, normalized nonlocal form, spacetime estimate or modified energy may still repair the leakage
